name: CarouselBot
summary: AI tool that turns a topic or an article into LinkedIn and Instagram carousels, single social cards, branded long-form documents and batch content sets, in four aspect ratios with your own brand settings.
best_for: solo creators, consultants and small marketing teams who post LinkedIn and Instagram carousels every week and want to turn articles and ideas into branded slides without designing them by hand
skip_if: you want free-form layouts in a full design tool; you need scheduling and publishing in the same app, which the pricing page does not list; or you post a carousel only now and then and the watermark-free plans are more than you need
honest_knock: Free exports carry a watermark (in our test on 18 November 2026 a small logo in the slide footer), and the free card sets, batch and document are lifetime totals, not monthly. Creator allows only 3 batches a month. The refund window is 7 days, the cards do not name their currency, and Business is only a starting price.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-11-25 on carouselbot.app/pricing in a headless browser, Annual view with the FAQ: prices, limits and the 7-day money-back guarantee unchanged, and the Save 34% and Save 31% labels match twelve monthly payments of $10 and $30, our arithmetic; read 2026-11-18 in a browser on carouselbot.app/pricing, Monthly and Annual views; earlier: read 2026-10-17; the cards show a $ sign without naming the currency) Free is $0 forever: 3 carousels a month, plus 3 card sets, 1 batch collection and 1 document in total, 3 AI images, up to 2,500 words per document, and PNG, JPG and PDF exports with a watermark. In our test (18 Nov 2026) the free app showed the same allowances (3 carousels, 3 card sets, 1 batch, 1 document), and the watermark was a small CarouselBot logo in the slide footer, not a large mark across the slide. Creator is $10 a month, or $79 a year on annual billing (shown as $6.58 a month): unlimited carousels, 3 card sets, 3 batches and 10 documents a month, up to 5,000 words per document, no watermark. Pro is $30 a month, or $249 a year (shown as $20.75 a month): unlimited card sets, batches and documents, up to 10,000 words per document. The annual cards cross out $120 and $360, twelve monthly payments. Business is a starting price of $50 a month for agencies and teams, adding bulk creation from up to 50 URLs; its final price and billing are not stated. The FAQ offers a 7-day money-back guarantee on all paid plans, requested by email; after cancelling you keep access until the billing period ends, then drop to Free, and saved work stays in your library.

compare_with.name: Piktochart
compare_with.why: Piktochart is in our dossiers too: a template-based maker for infographics, reports and posters, with a free plan and Pro at $10 per member a month billed yearly when we read it on 19 September 2026. CarouselBot is narrower and more automatic: it generates the slides for social carousels and cards from your text, priced per account rather than per member.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested CarouselBot in the existing Free our account: a carousel of 6 slides from a topic was ready in about 20 seconds and 3 steps, the headline and the template were changed with a click, and the PDF took about 10 seconds and was 113 KB. The common brewing tips are right, but the AI made up a figure (98% Of Coffee Flavor Comes From Water Quality) and a company claim (Test Co roasts in small batches). Free counted 1 of 3 carousels and only a small CarouselBot logo was seen on page 1 of the PDF, no large watermark. The prices match the dossier; the Annual view shows $6.58 and $20.75 a month and the dossier does not mention the 3 card sets and 1 batch on Free. There is no cancel button on the account page. The test carousel is still in the library, because the delete click was refused. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing Free our account, already signed in, with the interface in English (no language setting was found). The test started at about 11:16 with the welcome pop-up Welcome to CarouselBot!, which was skipped. The product is the same as the dossier domain (the page title is CarouselBot, Create LinkedIn Carousels in 2 Minutes) and the footer names a person as the maker; that name is not recorded here. The dossier name is CarouselBot and the review is on MSS (carouselbot-review); the handson folder and the review slug are the same. Usage on Free at the start: 1/3 carousels, 0/3 card sets, 0/1 batches, 0/1 documents, 0/3 AI images (manual) and 0/1 diagrams. Core action: a carousel from a topic. The input was 5 tips for brewing better coffee at home, for the fictional coffee brand Test Co, with 6 slides, the Warm template and Title Case. The form also offers Include AI-generated diagrams (BETA, 1 free), Include data charts and Include impact slides; none was turned on. The progress bar said Generating slide 5 of 6 and This usually takes 10-20 seconds; the result was there after about 20 seconds and 3 steps (topic, Continue, edit). AI text: slide 3 holds common tips (195 to 205 degrees Fahrenheit and 1 gram to 16 grams of water) that are right. Two things are made up: slide 2 says 98% Of Coffee Flavor Comes From Water Quality, a figure that exists nowhere (coffee is mostly water, but not this percentage), and slide 4 says Test Co roasts in small batches, a company claim nobody gave. Slides 5 and 6 are general and marketing like. The style reads smoothly with no language mistakes. Editing: through Edit Page 1 of 6 the headline was changed to Test Co: Better Home Coffee in 5 Steps (tabs Content, Icon and Image, Regenerate Copy, bold text and accent words); the template was switched from Warm to Ocean with one click; the ratios are 4:5, 1:1 and 9:16; a logo upload and a handle are available. Export: Download offers PDF Single file, PNG ZIP of images and JPG ZIP of images. The PDF said Rendering PDF... for about 10 seconds and was 113 KB, followed by Your carousel is downloaded! and Saved to your library!. The design is readable, with a large headline and enough contrast on Ocean. At the bottom of every slide is the small CarouselBot logo with an arrow; the pricing page says Free exports with a watermark, but only this small logo was seen and no large watermark. Only page 1 of the PDF was looked at. No name of the maker is on the slides. Plans, read on the pricing page (US dollars, nothing clicked): Free $0 forever (3 carousels per month, 3 card sets total, 1 batch collection total, 1 document total, 3 AI images, All templates, PNG, JPG and PDF export with watermark); Creator $6.58 a month on the Annual view ($120, $79 a year, Save 34%; the FAQ says $10 a month; Unlimited carousels, 3 card sets and 3 batches a month, 10 documents a month, Unlimited AI images and diagrams, No watermark, Custom branding with logo and handle); Pro $20.75 a month on the Annual view ($360, $249 a year, Save 31%; the FAQ says $30 a month; unlimited card sets, batches and documents, up to 10,000 words per document, priority help); Business $50 a month as a starting price (bulk creation of up to 50 URLs, advanced template customization, auto-apply branding and a Claude integration (MCP), Book a demo). A newsletter offer gives $50 off Annual plans, and there is a 7-day money-back guarantee on all paid plans. Against the dossier: the prices match and no scheduling or publishing was seen. Free also lists 3 card sets and 1 batch, and the Annual view shows $6.58 and $20.75 a month. Checkout: NOT reached. No upgrade button was clicked, so no tax, total, card or payment screen was seen. Cancelling: on the account page only the email address, the plan, the usage and Upgrade are shown, with no button to cancel or delete the account (there is no paid subscription); the FAQ says Cancel anytime from your account page. Not tested: the paid plans, AI diagrams, data charts, AI images, cards, batch, documents, URL input, a second carousel, PNG and JPG export, and scheduling or publishing (connecting an account was not allowed).
exit_test.awkward: The AI wrote a made-up figure (98% Of Coffee Flavor Comes From Water Quality) and a made-up company claim (Test Co roasts in small batches), so every slide has to be checked before posting. The pricing page says Free exports with a watermark, but only a small logo was seen. The account page has no button to cancel or delete the account, and the test carousel could not be removed from the library in this test.

exit_test.what: We created the account and our AI assistant ran the test in our browser. On 18 November 2026 the session tested CarouselBot in the existing Free our account: a carousel of 6 slides from a topic was ready in about 20 seconds and 3 steps, the headline and the template were changed with a click, and the PDF took about 10 seconds and was 113 KB. The common brewing tips are right, but the AI made up a figure (98% Of Coffee Flavor Comes From Water Quality) and a company claim (Test Co roasts in small batches). Free counted 1 of 3 carousels and only a small CarouselBot logo was seen on page 1 of the PDF, no large watermark. The prices match the dossier; the Annual view shows $6.58 and $20.75 a month and the dossier does not mention the 3 card sets and 1 batch on Free. There is no cancel button on the account page. The test carousel is still in the library, because the delete click was refused. No plan was bought. Account and start: the test used the existing Free our account, already signed in, with the interface in English (no language setting was found). The test started at about 11:16 with the welcome pop-up Welcome to CarouselBot!, which was skipped. The product is the same as the dossier domain (the page title is CarouselBot, Create LinkedIn Carousels in 2 Minutes) and the footer names a person as the maker; that name is not recorded here. The dossier name is CarouselBot and the review is on MSS (carouselbot-review); the handson folder and the review slug are the same. Usage on Free at the start: 1/3 carousels, 0/3 card sets, 0/1 batches, 0/1 documents, 0/3 AI images (manual) and 0/1 diagrams. Core action: a carousel from a topic. The input was 5 tips for brewing better coffee at home, for the fictional coffee brand Test Co, with 6 slides, the Warm template and Title Case. The form also offers Include AI-generated diagrams (BETA, 1 free), Include data charts and Include impact slides; none was turned on. The progress bar said Generating slide 5 of 6 and This usually takes 10-20 seconds; the result was there after about 20 seconds and 3 steps (topic, Continue, edit). AI text: slide 3 holds common tips (195 to 205 degrees Fahrenheit and 1 gram to 16 grams of water) that are right. Two things are made up: slide 2 says 98% Of Coffee Flavor Comes From Water Quality, a figure that exists nowhere (coffee is mostly water, but not this percentage), and slide 4 says Test Co roasts in small batches, a company claim nobody gave. Slides 5 and 6 are general and marketing like. The style reads smoothly with no language mistakes. Editing: through Edit Page 1 of 6 the headline was changed to Test Co: Better Home Coffee in 5 Steps (tabs Content, Icon and Image, Regenerate Copy, bold text and accent words); the template was switched from Warm to Ocean with one click; the ratios are 4:5, 1:1 and 9:16; a logo upload and a handle are available. Only page 1 of the PDF was looked at. No name of the maker is on the slides.
